newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Bush to announce summit on volunteerism.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Bush to announce summit on volunteerism.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and former President George Bush on Friday were set to announce that a three-day summit on community service will take place in Philadelphia in April, the White House said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the summit would be chaired by retired Gen. Colin Powell, former chairman of the military Joint Chiefs of Staff, and that its aim was to "bring together in a bipartisan way people who are committed to making this a better and stronger nation."

"Consistently throughout his tenure, he (Clinton) has called on Americans to work together to improve communities ... (the summit) will remind Americans of the importance of service and can be a way in which the president and his predecessors can help build a stronger America," McCurry said.
White House officials said the summit would occur April 27-29, and that former Presidents Gerald Ford and Jimmy Carter had also agreed to participate.

McCurry said Clinton was delighted that Bush, who promoted volunteerism during his presidency through his "Points of Light" programme, was willing to help launch the summit. Clinton and Bush were to do so at a 2:45 p.m. EST (1945 GMT) White House ceremony that Powell was also to attend.
